categories.main_business_segments: Chevron operates two primary business segments: Upstream and Downstream. The Upstream segment focuses on the exploration, development, production, and transportation of crude oil and natural gas, as well as liquefied natural gas (LNG), carbon capture, and gas-to-liquids. The Downstream segment encompasses refining crude oil into petroleum products, marketing fuels and lubricants, manufacturing and marketing renewable fuels, petrochemicals, and fuel/lubricant additives. Additionally, Chevron has significant interests in chemicals (through Chevron Phillips Chemical Company and Chevron Oronite) and new energies businesses.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Chevron employs advanced technologies in deepwater drilling, shale and tight oil recovery, LNG processing, and factory-style multi-well pad development. The company utilizes hydraulic fracturing, horizontal drilling, carbon capture and storage, and digital/data science for operational efficiency. In Downstream, Chevron leverages complex refining processes, renewable fuel production (including biodiesel, renewable diesel, and RNG), and advanced chemical manufacturing. The company also invests in emerging technologies such as hydrogen production, geothermal, and AI-driven operational improvements.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Chevron serves a broad range of customers including industrial, commercial, and retail consumers. Key markets include transportation (fuels and lubricants), power generation (natural gas and LNG), petrochemical manufacturers, and aviation (jet fuel). The company supplies products to branded service stations, commercial and industrial clients, and through trading operations, with significant presence in the U.S., Asia-Pacific, and other international markets.
categories.geographic_coverage: Chevron has a global footprint with operations and projects in North America (notably the U.S. Permian and DJ Basins, Gulf of Mexico), South America (Argentina, Brazil, Canada), Africa (Angola, Nigeria, Equatorial Guinea), Asia (Bangladesh, Israel, Kazakhstan, Thailand), Australia (Gorgon and Wheatstone LNG), and Europe (UK North Sea). The company’s largest reserves are in the U.S., Australia, and Kazakhstan, with significant downstream and marketing operations in the U.S., Asia-Pacific, and select international locations.
categories.supply_chain_position: Chevron is an integrated energy company operating across the entire value chain. In Upstream, it is primarily upstream (exploration and production), but also participates in midstream (transportation, storage, pipelines, LNG shipping). In Downstream, Chevron is active in refining (midstream/downstream), product marketing, and chemicals manufacturing, as well as renewable fuels and power generation. The company also invests in new energies and carbon management, positioning itself across traditional and emerging energy supply chains.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Chevron’s strategic focus is to deliver higher returns and lower carbon, leveraging its strengths to lead in lower carbon intensity oil, products, and natural gas, while advancing new energy solutions. The company is investing in renewable fuels, carbon capture and storage, hydrogen, power for data centers, and emerging technologies. R&D priorities include digital transformation, AI, advanced drilling and production, emissions reduction, and scaling new energy businesses. Chevron has committed approximately $10 billion through 2028 for lower carbon investments and continues to pursue innovation through internal development and external partnerships.
categories.revenue_model: Chevron generates revenue primarily through the sale of crude oil, natural gas, LNG, refined petroleum products, petrochemicals, and lubricants. Additional revenue streams include renewable fuels, trading activities, licensing, and equity earnings from affiliates. The company also earns income from chemicals manufacturing, pipeline transportation, and power generation, with a growing focus on new energy solutions and carbon management services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Chevron competes with major integrated oil and gas companies (such as ExxonMobil, Shell, BP, and TotalEnergies), national oil companies, and independent producers in both upstream and downstream sectors. In chemicals, it competes with global chemical manufacturers. Chevron is positioned as one of the world’s largest publicly traded energy companies, with a strong presence in North America, Asia-Pacific, and other key regions, and is recognized for its operational scale, technological capabilities, and growing focus on lower carbon solutions.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, Chevron reported sales and operating revenues of $193.4 billion and net income attributable to Chevron of $17.7 billion. The company produced 3.3 million barrels of oil-equivalent per day and had total assets of $256.9 billion at year-end. While revenues and earnings declined from 2022 highs due to lower commodity prices, Chevron maintains a strong balance sheet, robust free cash flow, and continues to invest in both traditional and lower carbon businesses. The company anticipates 6-8% production growth in 2025 (excluding asset sales) and is executing a significant capital return program.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Chevron emphasizes reliable, affordable, and increasingly lower carbon energy solutions, leveraging its operational excellence, global scale, and technological innovation. The company differentiates itself through its integrated value chain, strong safety and environmental performance, leadership in digital and advanced technologies, and commitment to shareholder returns. Chevron’s growing portfolio of renewable fuels, carbon management, and new energy businesses positions it as a leader in the energy transition while maintaining competitive strengths in traditional oil, gas, and chemicals.
